stem: A client with cancer is ambulatory and independently performs self-care but can no longer work and is up and active for more than half of each waking day. Which ECOG performance-status grade best matches this description?
rationale: The ECOG Performance Status Scale classifies functional impairment based on self-care, activity, ambulation, and time spent out of bed or chair. ECOG 2 describes a person who is ambulatory and capable of self-care but unable to perform work activities and is up for more than 50% of waking hours. ECOG 0 indicates full activity; ECOG 1 indicates restriction in strenuous activity while retaining ability to perform light or sedentary work; ECOG 3 indicates only limited self-care and confinement to bed or chair for more than half of waking hours. Performance status is used to describe and track functional status and may inform clinical-trial eligibility, treatment planning, and prognosis, but it does not replace the rest of the clinical assessment.
educational_objective: Apply the ECOG Performance Status Scale to functional assessment by correctly identifying ECOG 2 from ambulation, self-care capacity, inability to work, and time active during waking hours.

source_claim_supported: ECOG-ACRIN defines ECOG 2 as ambulatory and capable of self-care but unable to carry out work activities and up more than 50% of waking hours. ECOG performance status describes functional impairment and can be used to assess functional change, treatment context, and prognosis.

correction_summary: Rebuilt the original definition-only ECOG/Karnofsky item into an applied ECOG scoring scenario using the primary ECOG-ACRIN scale. Removed the broad claim that performance status directly determines tolerance for aggressive therapy and avoided mixing two different scoring systems in one construct. The final item tests accurate functional classification while preserving that performance status supplements rather than replaces clinical assessment.
audit_findings: Original item mixed ECOG and Karnofsky scales and tested only a broad purpose statement rather than application of a standardized assessment tool.
Fresh primary-source review of ECOG-ACRIN directly supports the functional criteria used in the stem and uniquely maps them to ECOG 2.
The final item does not claim that one performance-status score alone determines treatment selection or prognosis.
Distractors are adjacent ECOG grades rather than obviously unrelated concepts, improving discrimination without creating ambiguity.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct grade with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported treatment inference, or unresolved source conflict.
